text:
Marathon Petroleum stock gained nearly 8% over two weeks and added another 0.3% today, riding a sharp upward move since August 28th. The immediate backdrop is tightening refinery conditions: U.S. refineries are running at 98% capacity, and diesel prices hit record highs this week as Ukraine and Iran conflicts have knocked refineries offline globally—including Russian facilities forced to halt exports. For a major U.S. refiner like this company, constrained supply and higher refined product prices translate directly to wider profit margins on what they produce and sell.

Geopolitical escalation in the Middle East adds upside pressure. Intensifying sanctions on Iran, EU backing for these measures, and military positioning around the Strait of Hormuz all narrow the window for crude supply, keeping oil prices elevated (U.S. crude at $91/barrel, world crude at $96/barrel). Higher crude combined with refinery bottlenecks means refiners can charge more for gasoline and diesel relative to their input costs—the engine of refining profits.
